value: Whether novel relational information presented below awareness is stored well enough to bias a conscious decision made twenty minutes later.

Can novel relational information delivered subliminally, after only one or two encoding episodes and without any intention to process it, be stored long enough to bias conscious decisions 15-25 minutes later?

Two masked-stimulation experiments show that single or double subliminal exposures to novel face-occupation and pseudoword-translation pairs shift later conscious decisions above chance, with no significant decay between a 15- and a 25-minute delay.

quote: We ran two experiments to test whether subliminal stimulus pairs would affect delayed decision-making ( Figure 1a ).
This is unprecedented evidence of the longevity and impact of subliminal messages on conscious, rational decision-making.
